introduction.title: Readi Platform Documentation
introduction.description: Official documentation for Readi — drone operations and compliance platform.

blocks.text: Welcome to the official documentation for **Readi**, an operations and compliance platform for drone teams.

Readi helps aviation and drone operations teams manage planning, missions, training, compliance, maintenance, and records in one workspace. It is built for day-to-day operations while keeping your team audit-ready and giving everyone visibility of safety.

This documentation is written for the people who use Readi: pilots, operations managers, maintenance staff, safety and compliance managers and administrators. You do not need technical knowledge. The **Business Logic** and **Platform Rules** sections go deeper for people who want to know exactly how a rule works.
What you can do in Readi

items: Request evaluations and plan missions, with approvals and flight requests
Run operations on a daily board and calendar, with weather help and D-Flight authorization
Record every flight, battery and incident in the logbooks
Manage drones and their components, and keep them airworthy with maintenance tickets
Keep documents with versions, and link them to the equipment they apply to
Run compliance with evidence tracking, audit plans and safety targets
Track safety indicators and see your Safety Health Index
Organise personnel, departments, qualifications, procedures and checklists
Manage training courses, certificates and expiry dates
Get alerts in one inbox, and ask questions to the AI assistant

rows: [Operations](/docs/modules/operations) (declaration, Daily Board, completing a mission), then [Logbooks](/docs/modules/logbooks)

getting-started.title: Getting Started
getting-started.description: A step-by-step first-day and first-week guide to setting up Readi.

blocks.text: This guide takes you from a new account to your first completed mission. Do the steps in order, because each one builds on the one before.
Day 1: get in and secure your account

items: **Activate your account** with the link in the invitation email, then sign in.
**Set up two-factor authentication** with an authenticator app when Readi offers it after your first password change.
**Set your Authorization PIN** under **Settings → Security**. You need it to start and finish missions.
Open your **Profile** and check your name, timezone and department.
**Company:** check the company details, logo and timezone ([Company](/docs/configuration/company)).
**Team:** invite your people, give each a role and a department, and add pilot qualifications ([Team Management](/docs/configuration/team)).
**Clients:** add the clients you fly for.
**Mission Definitions:** adjust the mission types, categories, statuses and results to your needs ([Mission Definitions](/docs/configuration/mission-definitions)).
**Organisation:** add procedures, checklists, assignments and communication protocols ([Procedures, Assignments and Communication](/docs/configuration/procedures-assignments)).
Add each **system** (drone) and its **components**, with serial numbers ([Systems](/docs/modules/systems)).
Organise the parts with **Relations** and choose the **primary component**.
If you use D-Flight or Control Center, connect them so drones and flights come in automatically ([D-Flight](/docs/business-logic/dflight-integration), [Control Center](/docs/modules/flytbase)).
Upload manuals and certificates to the [Document Repository](/docs/records/document-repository).

blocks.text: Week 1: plan and fly your first mission

items: Send a **New Evaluation Request** and follow it to a positive result ([Planning](/docs/modules/planning)).
Create a mission in **Operations**, choose the drone, pilot and observers ([Operations](/docs/modules/operations)).
On the day, the pilot files the **daily declaration**, and the mission is moved across the **Daily Board** with the PIN.
When it is done, complete the mission: record component usage, attach the flight log and add the post-flight data.
Check the flight in the **Flight Logbook** ([Logbooks](/docs/modules/logbooks)).
Add a **training** record for each pilot and check the expiry dates ([Training](/docs/modules/training)).
Add one **compliance requirement** and attach evidence ([Compliance](/docs/modules/compliance)).
Define a **safety indicator** and log its first value ([Safety Management](/docs/modules/safety-management)).
Check **Maintenance** and open a test ticket to see how it works ([Maintenance](/docs/modules/maintenance)).
Read your **Notifications** every day ([Notifications](/docs/modules/notifications)).
Ask the [AI Assistant](/docs/modules/ai-assistant) when you cannot find something.
Review the [Audit Logs](/docs/records/audit-logs) now and then.
See [Release Notes](/docs/modules/releases) to learn what is new.

key-features.title: Key Features
key-features.description: Overview of Readi core feature areas.

rows: Flight plan creation, approval workflow, waypoints, test logbooks
Kanban board, daily calendar, mission execution tracking
Flight logbooks with filtering by pilot, drone, date, type
Drone and equipment inventory, component lifecycle, maintenance tickets
Incident reports, hazard observations, corrective actions, KPI tracking
Audit records, regulatory requirements, evidence upload
Tickets with technician reports, evidence and automatic counter reset
Versioned documents linked to several components, with change log
One inbox with categories and filters
Role-scoped natural language queries over mission, maintenance, and compliance data

items: Operational status (`OPERATIONAL / MAINTENANCE / NOT_OPERATIONAL`) is computed live on every fleet load — not stored
Mission status changes require a cryptographic **Authorization PIN** — every transition is signed and auditable
The AI Agent enforces row-level security — pilots only see their own data

system-requirements.title: System Requirements
system-requirements.description: What you need on your computer or phone to use Readi without problems.

blocks.text: Readi runs in your web browser, so there is nothing to install. You need a recent browser and a working internet connection.
If something looks wrong or a button does nothing, update your browser first. It fixes most problems.
Readi works on a computer, tablet or phone. Tables and maps are easiest to use on a larger screen. On a phone, the Daily Board and Calendar are shown one day at a time.

items: A stable connection is needed. Maps, the weather forecast and live flight data are loaded as you use them.
If your company uses a firewall or proxy, ask your IT team to allow Readi and its email service. Otherwise pages, maps or emails may not load.

blocks.text: Permissions your browser may ask for

rows: Only if you use the crosshair button on a map to use your current position. You can also search for a place or tap the map instead
Allow them for Readi, because some PDFs and documents open in a new tab
Needed for exports and reports, such as the QTB report, logbook exports and document downloads
25 MB, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, JPG, PNG or TXT
100 MB each, JPG, PNG, MP4 or PDF

items: You need an **authenticator app** on your phone (such as Google Authenticator or Authy) to set up two-factor authentication. See [Settings and Security](/docs/configuration/settings-security).
You need an **email address** that you can read, to receive your activation link.

blocks.text: Features are limited by role, so make sure each person has the right role before you give them access. See the [Role Glossary](/docs/business-logic/role-glossary).

legend: **R** = read, **W** = write / edit, **D** = delete. – = no access.
* Delete also requires the user's **Manager** flag. ¹ Can add new records but cannot edit existing ones.

† Fixed, not editable: ADMIN, OPM and SUPERADMIN always have full access; RM and SLA follow built-in rules; CLIENT only uses the Client Portal. For the other roles, **Yes** means the access level can be switched between read-only (R) and full (R · W · D) in **Team → Roles & Permissions**, which only ADMIN, OPM and SUPERADMIN can open. A role with no access (–) cannot be changed there. A user with individual custom permissions follows those instead of their role.
